title: Oncall patterns and SLO synthesis - week of 2027-03-01
body:
Purpose:
Weekly synthesis for the SRE team focusing on emergent on-call patterns, current SLO health, and prioritized follow-ups from recent incidents. This is intentionally conversational — notes to self, open questions for engineering owners, and concrete actions for the on-call rotation list.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (note taker, on-call this week)
- Jonas Eriksson (infra)
- Mei Lin (serving runtime)
- Ravi Kapoor (platform eng)
- Tara Gomez (SRE rotation lead)

TL;DR:
- Three small/medium incidents this week (network flaps + autoscaler misfire + degraded KV-cache hit rate). No customer-facing outages but increased latency on Preview and Dedicated endpoints during peak.
- Global SLOs: availability steady at 99.985% (30d), p99 latency drifted from 310ms -> 370ms for short-context requests — root cause tied to degraded KV cache hit rate on a subset of hosts.
- On-call handoff friction noted: missing explicit escalation steps in the autoscaler runbook and unclear owner for the 'fallback-to-quantized' policy.
- Actions: update autoscaler runbook, instrument more granular cache metrics, add canary for fallback policy, and schedule a 2-hour post-incident triage with serving-runtime + infra owners.

Incident summaries (concise):
1) Incident: SRE-4982 - regional network flap (2027-03-01 02:40-03:10 UTC)
   - Impact: transient increase in request error rate ~1.2% for eu-west hosts, traffic re-routed by smart-router with ~30s of elevated latencies.
   - Detection: alert from network-health (pager) + downstream user error spikes.
   - Root-cause (preliminary): a transit provider reconfiguration caused BGP route churn; our fallback routing engaged but overwhelmed a few edge proxies.
   - Mitigation: manual traffic steering to alternate fabric and warm-up of spare edge proxies.
   - Follow-ups: add automated backoff for router reconfiguration steps (owner: Jonas), add a synthetic that exercises failover every 12h (owner: Mei).

2) Incident: SRE-5001 - autoscaler mis-evaluation leading to temporary underprovision (2027-03-02 11:10-11:45 UTC)
   - Impact: slight queueing at batch ingress, burst latency for long-context generation increased to p95 ~1.6s (from baseline ~900ms). No dropped requests but client retries observed.
   - Detection: autoscale anomaly alert + increased queue-depth alerts on dedicated-pool-7.
   - Root-cause (prelim): recent tuning change to scaling cooldown (PR #3762) made the policy too conservative for sudden burst patterns. Metric smoothing delayed scale-up.
   - Mitigation: temporary override scaling thresholds to aggressive profile (manual), roll back PR #3762.
   - Follow-ups: add an automated 'burst-detect' heuristic (owner: Ravi), add a canary for scaling policy changes (owner: Tara), include rollback playbook steps in the autoscaler runbook.

3) Degradation: elevated KV cache miss rate on a subset of dedicated-serving hosts (ongoing, noticed 2027-03-02 onwards)
   - Impact: p99 latency for short prompts increased (~+60ms across calls where cache is helpful). Affects hosted-preview regionally.
   - Hypothesis: partial loss of local cache warm state after a rolling maintenance combined with eviction policy mismatch for certain model sizes.
   - Short-term mitigation: increase cache generosity on the impacted hosts and trigger a controlled re-warm (owner: Mei).
   - Follow-ups: expose per-host cache-hit SLI in Grafana, add alert for sustained miss-rate >10% for >30m, evaluate adopting a clustered shared KV-cache for high-churn models.

SLO status and observations:
- Global availability SLO (99.97% monthly): current 30d: 99.985% — within target but with narrow margin.
- Latency SLO (p99 <= 400ms for short-context endpoints): 30d p99 = 358ms, 7d p99 = 372ms. Trend lines show spikes aligned with autoscaler/kv-cache events.
- Error budget consumption: monthly budget pace is steady; two events consumed ~0.02% each — flagged but not urgent.
- Observability gaps: we lack high-cardinality SLI slices for deduplicating 'route level' vs 'host-level' latency. Need per-route + per-host breakdown. Owner: Jonas + Observability team.

On-call handoff notes (operational friction found):
- Yesterday's handoff was missing the explicit escalation path for TTL cache corruption. The on-call doc references 'eng pager' but not the paged-on-call rotation; add direct Slack alias + escalation windows to runbook (owner: Tara).
- Handoff checklist proposed additions:
  1) Current active incidents and short summary (1-2 lines)
  2) Any suppressed alerts and why
  3) Recent deploys (last 24h) + PR IDs
  4) Pending owner actions and expected ETA
- Action: produce a 1-page handoff template and land it in Confluence, then require it in rotations for 2 weeks to gather feedback. (owner: Aisha).

Action items (concrete):
- [Aisha] Draft on-call handoff template + example (due 2027-03-05).
- [Jonas] Implement synthetic failover test to exercise alternate fabric; add to CI schedule (due 2027-03-18).
- [Mei] Surface per-host KV-cache-hit metrics; implement alerting rule for sustained miss-rate (due 2027-03-10).
- [Ravi] Design and spec burst-detect scaling heuristic; schedule spike-testing in staging (due 2027-03-15).
- [Tara] Add autoscaler rollback steps to the runbook and prototype canary flow for scaling policy PRs (due 2027-03-12).
- [Infra + Observability] Investigate adding higher-cardinality SLI slices (path + host) and estimate cost/retention impact (owner: Jonas, due 2027-03-22).

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we want to maintain a 'grace capacity' reservoir for sudden bursts, or rely on faster scale-up heuristics? (ops cost vs risk tradeoff). Tentative preference: hybrid (small reserved + heuristic); more modeling needed.
- Should the KV-cache be shared for hot models vs local-only? Risks: cross-host contention vs faster warm for local caches. Explore prototype for a small model set.

Notes-to-self / rough brainstorming (informal):
- Consider adding a 'micro-canary' that runs a tiny, realistic generation workload on any rollout of autoscaler or routing logic. It should mimic traffic distribution between short and long contexts.
- Could we tag models with 'warmth expectation' metadata that informs eviction policy? (e.g., models used by Conversational flows marked high-warmth).

Next steps / meeting cadence:
- Schedule 2 hour post-incident triage (SRE + serving-runtime + infra) for SRE-5001 / KV-cache mismatch: target 2027-03-04 16:00 UTC (owner: Aisha to book).
- Follow-up SLO health check snapshot in next weekly notes (include new per-host views).
- Revisit on-call handoff checklist after 2 rotations (owner: Tara).

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- SRE-4982 (network flap) - https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-4982
- SRE-5001 (autoscaler) - https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-5001
- Autoscaler PR referenced: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3762
- Grafana SLO dashboard (ops): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/slo-overview?orgId=1

If you skim only one thing: prioritize the autoscaler rollback runbook and the cache per-host metrics. Both are low-effort but will prevent the two main classes of short-term regressions we saw this week.

-- Aisha
